newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses down, hit by interest rate fears.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses down, hit by interest rate fears.

text.p: European bourses ended the day mostly down on Thursday, disheartened by inflation worries and a poor performance by Wall Street after its record-breaking run.

On currency markets, the dollar was stronger against the yen, but off earlier highs reached after Japanese authorities shut down a troubled bank, the first time they have done so in five decades. Sterling also rose to its best level since 1992.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, registered a 0.25 percent loss at the close. The market was depressed by Wall Street's drop of 0.4 percent on profit-taking after closing at 6,430.02 points on Wednesday, the 10th record this month.
Domestic issues weighed heavily on bourses in Europe from the start of trading, decoupling them from the New York rally on Wednesday.
London investors were preoccupied by sterling's strength, interest rate fears and the possibility of unwelcome news in next week's budget.
The market feared that finance minister Kenneth Clarke might indulge in pre-election tax cuts in next Tuesday's budget despite rising inflationary pressures, analysts said.
"People are sitting on their hands, we've decoupled from Wall Street," said one senior trader. "They've laid out their stalls and battened down their hatches until after the budget."

Investors were still unsettled by British figures issued on Wednesday showing stronger-than-expected October retail sales, which reignited interest rate anxieties. The mood was not helped when figures on Thursday showed Britain's second quarter trade surplus was the best for 10 years.
"The data yesterday and today have encouraged people to anticipate a quarter-point rate rise before Christmas," one dealer said.

In Frankfurt, floor transactions ended in the minus column after listless trading which dealers said lacked direction. Computerised dealing on the IBIS DAX index was down two points in late trade at 2,763.10.

French shares clawed back losses to squeeze just into positive territory at the close after a bout of proofit-taking ahead of Friday's monthly settlement hit the market. Wall Street's sell-off also hit sentiment.
Volume was a heavy 6.1 billion francs.

The dollar was stronger against the yen but underlying support for the Japanese currency came from Japan's robust September diffusion index of leading indicators which showed the economy was continuing to recover gradually.
Currency traders were keeping a close eye on Japan's banking sector after the closure of Hanwa Bank Ltd, suffocating under 190 billion yen ($1.7 billion) in problem loans.
The dollar initially also strengthened against the mark after the Bundesbank's policy-making council on Thursday decided to leave German interest rates unchanged as expected.
Analysts said rates were likely to remain steady for some time given Thursday's weak German retail sales figures and a weak Ifo business outlook for 1997.
But a late burst of mark strength against other European curencies, particularly the French franc, was seen pressuring the dollar, eroding earlier gains in late trade.
Sterling had a good day, soaring more than two pfennigs against the mark to hit its best level since April 1994 and hitting a four-year high against the dollar.
The pound surged to 1.5030 marks and $1.6905 before falling back slightly at the close.
On bullion markets, gold closed at $376.65 an ounce, its lowest since March, 1995, after a technical sell-off sent prices spiralling.
Sentiment in the gold market has been increasingly gloomy in recent days since speculators were discouraged by the failure of a rally last week that peaked at just under $385 an ounce.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.43 yen and 1.4980 marks, compared with 111.17 yen and 1.4960 marks in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 9.0 points lower at 3,953.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 0.18 at 2,233.57.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 2.16 at 2,772.34.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $376.65 an ounce, compared with Wednesday's close of $379.15. Silver was at $4.87, down nine cents.
